A1.justification: Both PDFs are 38-page versions of the same paper. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original DiT, PixArt-α, and MMDiT experiments, including benchmark results, hyperparameter searches, and human text-image alignment evaluation in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and human-evaluation outcomes in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same µP implementation, attention-width scaling procedure, hyperparameter searches, and proxy-to-target transfer algorithm.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains identical: ImageNet, SA-1B/SAM, MS-COCO-30K, MJHQ-30K, GenEval, the internal image-text training dataset, and the 150-prompt human-evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same DiT-XL-2, PixArt-α, and MMDiT-18B baselines, including the appendix comparisons. Revised background references do not change the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training budgets, hyperparameter ranges, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain DiT evaluation on 50K samples without classifier-free guidance and the same human-evaluation design.

E4.justification: Both retain the transferability sweeps across widths, batch sizes, training steps, and output multipliers; the MMDiT proxy-duration check in Table 17; and the qualitative examples in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither introduces repeated-seed uncertainty summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests; Figure 10 retains the same statement about matching generation seeds.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and Appendix E. For example, Table 4 retains overall GenEval scores of 0.8154 and 0.8218, and Table 5 retains alignment accuracies of 0.703 and 0.715 for baseline and µP MMDiT respectively.

T1.justification: The µP scaling rules, definitions, assumptions, and proofs in Section 3 and Appendices B–C are unchanged. Reordering U-ViT and DiT in Theorems 3.1 and C.1 does not alter their mathematical scope.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diffusion Transformers share standard µP, hyperparameters transfer across scales, and tuning enables the reported convergence and computational-efficiency benefits.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning learning rates, clipping, generalization, and classifier-free guidance are retained, as is the unresolved optimal proxy-task-size limitation. Section 6 adds citations without changing its interpretations or proposed research directions.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware and training-time disclosures, asset licenses, and access information are unchanged. Table 7 and the project link retain the same resources despite citation renumbering.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 now explicitly places U-ViT before DiT, replacing the earlier DiT-first description and U-ViT's explicit connection to ViT. The ViT reference is removed, while three references on neural tangent kernels and mean-field dynamics are added to Section 6: v3 references 9, 51, and 58.

P1.justification: Changes comprise a localized rewrite of Section 2.1, reordered architecture lists, citation updates, and the new version date. The overall narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Reference changes produce limited bibliography reflow across pages 12–16, with minor wrapping changes in revised prose. All 10 figures and 17 tables retain their visual content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 revises the U-ViT/DiT historical presentation and adds literature pointers to existing future directions while removing the ViT reference. These localized edits leave the substantive exposition, theoretical support, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations essentially unchanged, without a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
